title: API incident decision log and runbook sketch
content:
Purpose and audience
--------------------
This is a working sketch: a compact, decision-centric runbook for the most common API failure patterns we face (client-visible timeouts, 429 throttles, degraded streaming, and rising 5xx/error rates). Primary audience: SREs on first/second-line oncall and engineers responding to live degradations.

Scope and assumptions
- Applies to hosted API and Dedicated ingress/fronting proxies; many of the operational checks are shared.
- Assumes access to SLO/alert dashboards, the api-gateway logs, runtime pod metrics, and routing layer traces.
- This is intentionally lightweight: quick checks, definite actions, and a short decision log.

Quick glossary (terms we use below)
- request-latency-p95/p99: production histograms in Datadog/Grafana for frontend request latency.
- infra-429: client receives HTTP 429 from gateway/proxy due to quota or upstream rejection.
- degraded-stream: streaming responses are partial, stalled, or repeatedly reconnecting.
- circuit-breaker: route-level breaker in the API gateway that trips after X errors.

Decision log (live, append-only)
- 2025-11-04 09:17 UTC — Decision: during a p95 spike, prefer immediate routing fallback to model-variant (smaller quantized) before global traffic split rollback; rationale: preserves throughput and avoids heavy cache invalidation. Owner: Mira C.
- 2025-12-10 03:11 UTC — Action: increased default backoff on client retries from 200ms->500ms after INF-4721 indicated amplification loop. Note: need to update SDK defaults. Owner: Jonah P.
- 2026-01-22 22:45 UTC — Observed streaming stalls tied to Nginx upstream buffering; temporary mitigation: disable proxy buffering for streaming routes. Owner: Leah G.

Triage checklist (first 10 minutes)
1) Confirm alert and scope: check Grafana alert dashboard; note which routes/models/regions are affected.
   - dashboards: API Overview -> Requests by route, Errors by route, Latency heatmap.
2) Identify client impact: Are external clients getting 5xx, 429, or timeouts? Request examples from the incident channel (copy raw request headers + timestamps).\3) Look for cross-correlation: Are infra metrics (host CPU/GPU, network IO, connection saturation) anomalous?\4) Check recent deploys/rollouts: rollout history in Console -> rollouts. If a canary was promoted within the last 30m, mark as suspect.

Common failure patterns and concrete actions
A) Timeouts (client-side request times out, server logs show long tail)\- Symptoms: request latency p95/p99 spikes; runtime token-generation step shows burst in decoder time; KV cache miss spike.\- First checks (CLI snippets):\  - kubectl get pods -n runtime -l app=inference -o wide\  - kubectl logs -n runtime -l app=inference --since=10m | rg "decode|token|OOM|latency"\  - curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <test-key>" -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":128}' --max-time 10\- Quick mitigations:\  - If KV/prefix cache miss rate jumped: route small percent of traffic to a cached-model variant (route config -> enable prefix cache)\  - If GPU saturation high (util > 85% across pool): start burst-capacity or shift to lower-cost model-variant; notify infra to add capacity if sustained.\  - If a recent rollout is suspect: rollback to previous revision (Console -> rollouts -> rollback).\- Longer-term notes: shorten default streaming chunk sizes for long-sequence workloads; investigate kernel selection heuristics for problematic models.

B) 429s (rate-limiting or upstream rejections)\- Symptoms: clients get 429s; gateway metrics show rate-limiter counters; per-customer quota logs spike.\- First checks:\  - Check gateway rate limiter metrics: rate_limiter.rejections.by_bucket (Grafana)\  - Confirm whether 429 originates at gateway or runtime (check x-origin header in response logs)\  - Identify client key(s): lookup API key in admin panel to see quotas/overrides.\- Actions:\  - If quota exceeded for specific key: contact customer-success if the client is high-value and create a temporary quota increase (documented TTL)\  - If global spike from noisy clients: apply short (1–3 min) soft-block on offending IP ranges via WAF and create ephemeral rule to observe effect\  - If upstream runtime returns 429 to gateway: enable fallback routing to alternate model pool or reduce request concurrency per-session via gateway config.\- Tuning heuristics (SRE notes): leaky-bucket windows should be >= 10s for bursty browser traffic; consider per-route vs per-api-key rate-limits.

C) Degraded streaming\- Symptoms: clients see partial streams, abrupt EOS, repeated reconnects, or long gaps between tokens.\- Immediate checks:\  - Is proxy buffering enabled? (Nginx/Envoy config)\  - Check connection counts and socket errors on edge LB\  - Runtime logs for stream-cancellation or client disconnects\- Quick mitigations:\  - Disable proxy buffering for streaming routes (edge-config -> streaming: buffering=false)\  - If TLS termination is overloaded, route streaming traffic to region with spare TLS-terminators\  - If model runtime is returning final chunk prematurely due to early EOS: enable safe-fallback to short-sentinel-generator variant\- Considerations: disabling buffering increases load on upstream; only apply per-route and monitor.

D) Elevated error rates (5xx spike)\- Symptoms: 502/503/500 counts increase, backend exceptions containing OOM, memalloc failures, or 2xx->4xx conversion in logs.\- First checks:\  - Check pod restarts (kubectl get pods -n runtime -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,RESTARTS:.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount)\  - Inspect runtime exception traces (s3/log-service or GCS) for repeated stack frames\- Actions:\  - If OOM/crashloop: scale down concurrency on route and redeploy with increased memory guardrails; consider rolling restart of affected pods.\  - If external dependency failing (auth, billing, quota service), flip fallback policy to degrade gracefully and return 502 with clear error body rather than 500.\  - If it's a transient resource pressure event: enable aggressive autoscaler profile for the affected pool and set temporary rollback on recent scaling decisions that may have reduced headroom.

Operational play primitives (things responders do, fast)\- Add a short-lived traffic filter in Console -> route -> filters (e.g., allow only internal keys)\- Toggle routing policy to fallback: Console -> routing -> set fallback=variant-x for 30m\- Increase model-pool capacity: infra->GPU pools->add-burst (requires infra SRE approval for >10% burst)\- Create temp alert suppression (10–30m) for noisy downstream alerts while investigating.

Oncall debugging commands (examples)
- kubectl top pods -n runtime --containers\- kubectl logs -n runtime -l route=chat-completion --since=5m -c runtime\- jq-based quick extractor for a sample request id in logs:\  - rg "request_id=([0-9a-f-]+)" | sed -n '1p' | xargs -I{} rg "{}" /var/log/runtime/* | head -n 200\- curl test against edge with verbose headers:\  - curl -v -H "X-Debug-Request: 1" -H "Authorization: Bearer <test>" 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat' -d @sample.json

Escalation checklist
- 0–15m: SRE oncall + listed responder.
- 15–30m: Pager duty escalation to SRE lead and infra oncall.
- 30+min: Ops war room, include product PM for high-customer-impact incidents and CS for affected accounts.
- Critical customer outage: engage support-engineering and AMs; follow the customer incident runbook.

Communications templates (short)
- Initial incident post (Slack): "INCIDENT: elevated 5xx on /v1/generate in us-east-1. Investigating — SRE oncall Mira C. Possible causes: recent model rollout or GPU pressure. Will update in 15m." 
- Customer-facing status blurb: "We are investigating elevated latency affecting some requests to generation endpoints. Working on mitigations; no confirmed data exposure. We'll post an update in 30 minutes."

Follow-ups and backlog items (for post-incident)
- Improve streaming observability: add per-token latency histogram and streaming-heartbeat metric.
- SDK defense: change client-side retry default to jittered exponential with max attempts=3 (follow-up PR: GH#2143).\- Experiment: route small percentage of traffic to quantized-INT8 variants during p95-only spikes and measure quality delta.
- Hardening: automate quick-fallback reroutes for model pool saturations (console action -> API endpoint).

Open questions / TODOs\- Default per-api-key quota vs per-route: should we shift to primarily per-route? Impact on noisy API key cases. (owner: Leah)\- How to signal SDK-level retry backoff changes to enterprise customers without causing throttles? (owner: Jonah)

Appendix: useful links and dashboards\- API Overview dashboard (Grafana) — /dashboards/api-overview\- Runtime pool health — /dashboards/runtime-pool-health\- Rollouts history — Console -> Rollouts\- Related Jira tickets: INF-4721 (retry amplification), INF-4899 (streaming stalls with proxy buffering)

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep this doc short. Ops deck is a different doc; link to it instead of copying.
- When we finalize: convert action items into checkboxes and add runbook automation playbooks for common switches (buffering toggle, fallback routing).

---
Draft end.
